demoScenario.title: Demo Scenario: Enterprise Authentication
demoScenario.description: Explore how three different products in an enterprise portfolio handle user authentication, revealing opportunities for standardization and optimization.

step1.label: Step 1
step1.title: Agent-Based Extraction
step1.description: AI agents automatically extract four ontology graphs (Code, Functional, Design, Architecture) from each product's codebase and documentation, creating structured knowledge graphs for analysis.

step2.label: Step 2
step2.title: Rationalization & Strategy Selection
step2.description: The extracted graphs are analyzed for overlaps, then split into parallel design and architecture rationalization tracks. Three implementation strategies are compared showing their respective code impact.

note.title: Note on Product-Specific Ontologies:
note.content: While the core rationalization framework focuses on the four primary ontologies (Code, Functional, Design, Architecture), real-world products often include additional product-specific ontologies such as user context graphs, master data models, workflows, and business rules. The rationalization strategy accommodates these product-specific data models by applying the same systematic analysis and consolidation principles to ensure complete unification without ambiguity.
